question: Why was the acid value of the macaw palm almond oil higher than every literature value for macaw oil it was compared with?
question_long: Why was the acid value of the macaw palm almond oil evaluated as a heat-transfer fluid higher than every literature value for macaw oil it was compared with?
expect: premise false: 3.44 mg KOH/g is slightly lower than Goncalves (3.49) and much lower than Melo (12.24) and Amaral (12.8)
rendered: The document does not state that the acid value of the macaw palm almond oil was higher than every literature value for macaw oil it was compared with. Instead, it states that the acid value of 3.44 mg KOH/g measured for the oil was lower than values reported by Gonçalves (3.49 mg KOH/g), Melo (12.24 mg of KOH/g), and Amaral (12.8 mg KOH/g), and below the "standard" acidity threshold of ∼5 mg KOH/g for acceptable-quality macaw oil.

prompt.system: You answer questions about one document, "Thermophysical and Chemical Evaluation of Macaw Palm Almond Oil as a Biobased Heat-Transfer Fluid Candidate for Medium-Temperature Solar Thermal Applications", using only what that document contains. It is below, condensed: page by page, the sentences that state a value, with the few other sentences that best match the question (the rest are left out), then its tables row by row and facts read from its figures. Answer briefly. If you compute a number, show the calculation. If the question assumes something the document contradicts, say so. If the document does not hold the answer, say so.
